dimensions.question: How clearly can a prospective Changi user determine which airport experience is actually available to them based on passenger state, terminal, public/transit location, immigration status, itinerary, baggage state and service-specific eligibility?
dimensions.scopeChange: None. Initial Case #40 public-evidence scope. The airport ecosystem is studied as hospitality infrastructure around passenger movement rather than as an airline product.

observations.text: The public airport interface explicitly distinguishes arriving, departing, transiting and visiting user states.
Transit eligibility depends on same-itinerary and through-checked-baggage conditions rather than physical presence in the airport alone.
Jewel, transit hotels, lounges and public-area facilities occupy materially different access states.
Dining and experiences are distributed by terminal and public/transit location rather than forming one universally accessible inventory.

unanswered: The evidence does not establish how successfully a first-time passenger understands public versus transit access before selecting a facility.
No systematic mobile-versus-desktop discovery audit has been completed.
No evidence establishes which hospitality discovery pathway creates the highest commercial contribution.
dimensions.reason: Public information exposes passenger, terminal and access-state distinctions, but decision clarity and commercial consequences remain unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Compare representative discovery paths for a transit hotel, public-area hotel/service, lounge, dining outlet, Jewel attraction and transit-only experience.

dimensions.question: What exactly becomes committed when a traveller books or accesses airport hospitality whose eligibility also depends on flight, itinerary, immigration, terminal, baggage, capacity or passenger-status conditions?
dimensions.scopeChange: The airport does not own the underlying airline reservation in this study. Reservation scope focuses on airport hospitality commitments and entitlement dependencies.

observations.text: A transit-hotel booking remains conditional on the guest preserving the correct airside immigration state.
Representative lounge access can be walk-in and credential-based while still remaining subject to capacity.
The Free Singapore Tour supports advance reservation but retains passenger, documentation, baggage, timing and availability conditions.
The Changi App supports booking or reservation functions for attractions and dining without establishing one shared inventory architecture across those services.
Air-carrier disruption and re-ticketing responsibility is separately identified in the official airport conditions document.

unanswered: No transit-hotel, lounge, attraction, dining or tour transaction was completed.
Cancellation, refund, no-show, capacity-failure and wrong-access-state recovery were not systematically tested.
The evidence does not establish whether separate airport hospitality reservations share one inventory, identity or recovery system.
dimensions.reason: Multiple airport hospitality commitments are visible, but their technical coupling, modification rules and failure recovery remain incomplete.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect booking conditions for representative hotel, lounge and attraction/tour products while keeping airline reservation ownership separate.

dimensions.question: What must a passenger resolve before reaching a Changi hospitality service, including flight status, terminal, itinerary, baggage, immigration, accessibility, onward boarding pass and service eligibility?

observations.text: Transit status requires specific itinerary and checked-baggage conditions, and some connecting passengers may instead need to enter Singapore and re-check.
Jewel access for a transit passenger requires arrival-immigration clearance, while some transit hospitality requires remaining airside.
Special-assistance preparation can require advance airline coordination even though airport assistance infrastructure is also available.
Flight, terminal and baggage information can be surfaced digitally before or during the airport journey.
Jewel early check-in and baggage services depend on their own eligibility and participating-airline conditions.

unanswered: Actual airline confirmations, hotel confirmations, lounge confirmations and airport notifications were not inspected end-to-end for one passenger journey.
The evidence does not establish whether accessibility, baggage, hotel and flight-status data remain synchronized across organisations.
Live disruption communication before airport arrival remains untested.
dimensions.reason: Pre-arrival preparation is visibly multi-party and state-dependent, but cross-system continuity remains unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Map one departing, one arriving and one connecting passenger's required pre-arrival information and responsible parties.

dimensions.question: Where does responsibility shift when a passenger arrives at Changi and must resolve immigration, transit status, terminal movement, baggage, onward boarding, accessibility and hospitality access?
dimensions.scopeChange: Arrival includes both arrival into Singapore and arrival into a connecting/transit operating state.

observations.text: A connecting passenger with an onward boarding pass can proceed toward the next gate, while one without it may first need a transfer desk.
Terminal movement differs by public/transit state and by terminal, with T4 requiring different transfer infrastructure from T1-T3.
Passenger assistance can involve airport Care Ambassadors, information counters and airline-arranged services rather than one universal assistance owner.
Baggage information can cross airport and airline systems, while baggage enquiries and airport-premises lost property route through different recovery channels.

unanswered: No immigration queue, transfer desk, baggage failure, terminal-transfer failure or assistance handoff was directly observed.
Recovery ownership for a passenger with a valid flight but incompatible baggage or access state remains incompletely mapped.
Actual transition from flight arrival to a lounge, hotel, Jewel or onward gate has not been observed.
dimensions.reason: Arrival clearly contains independent identity, baggage, mobility and access states, but live handoff quality remains unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Map a same-itinerary transfer, a self-managed transfer and a passenger entering Singapore to use Jewel, including failure branches.

dimensions.question: How do public/transit location, terminal, flight state, lounge access, hotel access, attractions, assistance and digital services coexist while a traveller spends time within the airport ecosystem?
dimensions.scopeChange: The required KHDS stay dimension is interpreted as airport dwell/participation for the airport institution, including layover, waiting and hospitality use.

observations.text: Airport dwell can include hotels, lounges, rest areas, attractions, dining and tours, but access depends on passenger and location state.
Public and transit areas can provide different mobility and hospitality options even within the same airport.
The Changi App can provide one digital surface across several journey and commercial functions without proving that the underlying operating systems are unified.
Assistance during airport participation can cross airport and airline responsibility boundaries.

unanswered: No representative layover or airport-dwell journey was observed.
The evidence does not establish re-entry, queue, capacity or recovery behaviour across all hospitality spaces.
Cross-terminal service continuity and handoff performance remain unverified.
dimensions.reason: The airport offers a broad hospitality ecosystem, but service continuity across access states and operators is not operationally established.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Compare one airside layover journey and one landside/public-area airport-dwell journey with explicit entitlement and responsibility states.

dimensions.question: How does dining access vary by terminal, public/transit state, lounge entitlement, traveller status, operating hours and reservation/payment pathway?

observations.text: Dining inventory is distributed across terminals, Jewel and public/transit operating areas.
A lounge can bundle food and beverage with a separate lounge-access entitlement.
A public-area venue can serve non-travellers while giving travellers a separate boarding-pass-linked commercial benefit.
The Changi App advertises dining discovery and reservation functions, creating a digital layer over separately operated outlets.

unanswered: No meal, lounge dining service or restaurant reservation was completed.
The evidence does not establish queue times, sold-out states, dietary-safety execution or cross-terminal dining recovery.
No comparative contribution data exists for public-area, transit, lounge or app-mediated dining.
dimensions.reason: Dining availability is visibly state- and location-dependent, but fulfilment, safety, capacity and economics remain unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Inspect representative public, transit and lounge dining pathways and separate discovery, reservation, access and fulfilment states.

dimensions.question: Where does the airport hospitality relationship end when flight departure, baggage, terminal transfer, disruption, airline recovery, digital tracking and post-service enquiries can continue beyond one physical space?
dimensions.scopeChange: Departure includes departure from a hospitality service, departure from Changi on a flight and unresolved responsibilities that can persist after physical movement.

observations.text: A departing or connecting passenger may still need security, terminal movement and onward-gate activity after leaving a hospitality service.
Baggage tracking can continue through loading and transfer states beyond the passenger's direct possession of the bag.
For flight delay or cancellation, Changi provides status information while rescheduling and compensation remain airline-facing matters.
The official conditions document assigns air carriers specified disruption, welfare, accommodation, re-ticketing and lost-baggage planning responsibilities.
Post-service enquiries can route differently to airlines, airport lost-and-found, Jewel or other channels.

unanswered: No missed connection, cancelled flight, missing bag, failed transfer or post-departure complaint was observed.
The evidence does not establish how quickly responsibility transfers among CAG, airlines, handlers and hospitality operators during disruption.
The 2017 Conditions of Use document requires current operational corroboration before being treated as a complete present-day operating description.
dimensions.reason: Departure strongly exposes persistent and distributed responsibility, but actual recovery performance remains unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Map disruption ownership for delay, cancellation, missed connection and baggage failure using current public evidence and operator-specific routes.

dimensions.question: How is the airport's hospitality atmosphere produced across transit hotels, lounges, public facilities, dining, Jewel, attractions and passenger-only spaces while access control remains active?

observations.text: The institution contains materially different rest, lounge, public recreation, dining and attraction environments rather than one uniform airport atmosphere.
Some hospitality environments are inseparable from passenger or immigration state, while public-area environments can also serve non-travellers.
Jewel intentionally combines attractions, retail, dining, hotel and luggage-related services in a public-area hospitality environment.

unanswered: Representative crowding, noise, privacy, rest quality and atmosphere across terminals were not directly observed.
No comparison of disruption-state versus normal-state atmosphere was completed.
The evidence does not establish whether intended atmosphere remains hospitable under high congestion or access failure.
dimensions.reason: Distinct hospitality environments are visible, but representative lived conditions remain unverified.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Compare one transit rest environment, one paid lounge, one public-area facility and Jewel using bounded public evidence.

dimensions.question: What can official imagery establish about terminal relationships, public/transit access, hotels, lounges, dining, Jewel, attractions and mobility, and what operational conditions remain invisible?

observations.text: The inspected source set identifies materially different visual subjects including terminals, transfer infrastructure, transit hotels, lounges, public facilities, dining and Jewel attractions.
Product and location distinctions require imagery to be interpreted by terminal and public/transit state rather than as generic Changi imagery.

unanswered: No systematic image-by-image photographic audit has been completed.
Official imagery does not establish queueing, crowding, security processing, accessibility fulfilment, baggage handoff or disruption recovery.
Image recency and representative ordinary operating conditions remain incompletely established.
dimensions.reason: The visual subjects are clear, but photographic evidence has not yet been systematically audited.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Perform a bounded image audit with terminal, public/transit, passenger-state and service-state labels.

dimensions.question: Does Singapore Changi Airport require a distinct hospitality responsibility architecture because passenger identity, flight status, terminal, airside/landside access, immigration, security, baggage and hospitality services cross multiple control boundaries, or can the observed structure be sufficiently explained as ordinary airport operations with passenger amenities layered on top?
dimensions.scopeChange: None. Initial Case #40 public-evidence scope. Ordinary airport operations plus passenger amenities remains the active competing explanation.

observations.text: One airport brand contains materially different arriving, departing, transiting and visiting passenger or visitor states.
Physical presence at Changi does not create universal entitlement because itinerary, baggage, immigration, terminal and public/transit state can alter what the person may access.
Airport hospitality can cross CAG, airline, government, lounge, hotel, concessionaire and other provider relationships rather than remaining under one apparent service owner.
A unified digital surface can expose flight, baggage, booking, dining, payment and reward functions without proving one underlying operational system.
Flight disruption, baggage recovery and passenger welfare expose explicit responsibility boundaries between airport and airline functions.
Public-area hospitality can serve visitors with no flight while other services require specific passenger and access states.

unanswered: The evidence does not establish whether Changi internally coordinates these states through one architecture or through conventional airport, airline and concession systems.
Live recovery across immigration, security, transfer, baggage, accessibility, lounge, hotel and flight disruption remains unverified.
No public evidence establishes causal performance superiority, comparative profitability or net contribution across hospitality pathways.
The 2017 Conditions of Use document requires bounded interpretation and current corroboration for any present-day operational claim.
dimensions.reason: Changi strongly exposes cross-system identity, entitlement and responsibility questions, but ordinary airport operations plus passenger amenities remains a sufficient competing explanation at public-evidence scope.
dimensions.nextEvidence: Test whether passenger identity, entitlement, information and recovery remain legible across airline, airport, immigration, baggage, terminal and hospitality transitions without assuming one integrated architecture.
